The webhook delivery logic is located in `/bench/repo/internal/webhook/webhook.go`.

`/bench/repo/internal/webhook/validate.go` likely contains the SSRF protection mechanism. `/bench/repo/smemo_service_webhooks.go` appears to trigger outbound HTTP on memo changes. Exact functions will be identified by reading these files.

Verifying the exact outbound HTTP delivery function and the mechanism blocking internal network address resolution.

The exact outbound HTTP delivery function is `Post` in `/bench/repo/internal/webhook/webhook.go`. The actual HTTP call runs at line 152 via `safeClient.Do(req)`. An async path uses `PostAsync` to enqueue jobs, and worker goroutines call `Post`.

The mechanism blocking internal network addresses is two-layer protection. `ValidateURL` in `validate.go` checks targets during registration and configuration by performing DNS lookups and applying `isReservedIP`.

The second layer is `safeDialContext` in `webhook.go`. It enforces `isReservedIP` at runtime through a custom `http.Transport` on `safeClient`. This checks against `reservedCIDRs` and `reservedNetworks` defined in `validate.go`.

The analysis is complete. I am structuring the precise answer with exact file paths and symbols.

The outbound HTTP delivery executes in `Post` within `/bench/repo/internal/webhook/webhook.go`. The actual HTTP request runs at `safeClient.Do(req)` on line 152. Async calls route through `PostAsync` in `memo_service_webhooks.go`, which queues payloads to worker goroutines that invoke `Post`.

SSRF protection operates at two stages.

Registration-time validation runs in `ValidateURL` inside `/bench/repo/internal/webhook/validate.go`. It performs a DNS lookup and rejects targets matching `isReservedIP` against `reservedCIDRs` and `reservedNetworks`.

Runtime delivery-time protection lives in `safeDialContext` inside `/bench/repo/internal/webhook/webhook.go`. It intercepts the `safeClient`'s `Transport.DialContext` to resolve hostnames at dial time and block reserved IPs, which defeats DNS rebinding.
